text:
**continue** (rechecked at 4a16771, after CL53b) · Land CL53. The orchestrator then reruns `install.py --update` on a scratch copy of ~/harmonize and opens a Claude Code session there: its first line must be CHECKOUT. That run (an install.py change) is the one thing not yet seen on the real project.

## Recheck after CL53b (origin/cl53 at 4a16771)
- `scripts/review/CR-cl53-a-session-always-starts-on-the-newest-co-new-branch.py` rerun: the new part branch stays on cl99 and the detached HEAD stays where it was. Each gets the line "behind … it has no commit of its own: `git checkout main && git merge --ff-only origin/main` if it is done (not switched: it may be a new branch)". The case is fixed.
- `tests.test_checkout_fresh`: 10 of 10 pass (2 new).
- Harmonize gap: `install.py` now adds a SessionStart line `kit.py fresh` to a Claude Code project whose own SessionStart does not run the kit hook. I read the code, but did not run it on Harmonize.
- Fresh merge of cl45 + cl51 + cl53 (b242c0f): one conflict, in the generated `.kit/artifact-files/files-board.json` files map only, which `land` or the next push will rewrite. With it resolved, `run_all_tests.py --all` gives **73 passed, 0 failed**.
- The trade-off, said once: the owner's ~/harmonize case (a merged branch, two days behind) is no longer switched to main by itself. Its first line now says so and gives the command. That is the safe reading, because "merged" and "new" look the same to git.

The text below is the first review (redirect), kept as written.

## Holds
**The 8 cases hold.**
- Check rerun: `python3 -m unittest tests.test_checkout_fresh -v`: 8 of 8 pass, with and without the web flag.
- Break (`revert`): kit.py and the hook taken back to 78df8a0: 1 failure, 7 errors.
- Recheck sample, "71 of 71 suites": on the merge with CL45 and CL51 (rebuilt here as f6fd14d, clean), `run_all_tests.py --all` gives **73 passed, 0 failed**.
- Real project (orchestrator, Harmonize): the merged branch was switched to main, 3 commits forward; a dirty branch was left as it was, with the edit kept.

**A case it gets wrong** (measured by `scripts/review/CR-cl53-a-session-always-starts-on-the-newest-co-new-branch.py`): `checkout_fresh` reads "no commit of its own" as "merged". It cannot tell a merged branch from a NEW one.
- A branch just made from a trunk that has moved since: "branch cl99 was merged into main: switched to main". HEAD ends on main.
- A detached HEAD on an older trunk commit (as a review worktree is): also switched to main.

On a computer, `kit.py launch` makes each part's worktree branch from the current branch, with no commits yet (`_make_worktree`). If the local trunk is behind origin at that moment (for example after a review's `land` pushed the trunk), the part's SessionStart runs `fresh` in that worktree:
- if main is checked out in the main checkout, git refuses, and the part's first line says it "could not be moved: do it by hand", which tells a part to go to main;
- if main is checked out nowhere, the part is put on main, and its commits go there.

**What he asked, on the real thing:** "At board start and at the first resume of any role, the kit … says, before anything else". On ~/harmonize, the owner's own case, a Claude Code session start says nothing. Harmonize's SessionStart is its own session-start.sh and does not run the kit hook (the orchestrator's real_project names the gap). Only a later `resume` prints CHECKOUT. A session opened there that works before resuming is still on old code without a word. That is the exact failure in the task (11-22 to 11-24), so this is a miss.

**With CL45 and CL51:** no contradiction in the code. All three split by platform the same way (web: CL53 does nothing, CL45 reconciles; computer: CL53 moves the checkout, CL51 keeps it off the Artifact). Only the detection differs: CL53 also counts KIT_REMOTE/AGY_REMOTE as web, while CL45 and CL51 count only CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE (see CR-cl51).

Not checked: Windows; a real part launched on a computer (I only rebuilt the git shape).

## Goal
The takeover train: any session, anywhere, starts from the newest state (board and code) without the owner noticing anything. CL53's measure (8 cases on temp repos) covers the checkouts it imagines. The owner's own example passes only halfway: the move works when `fresh` runs, but at Harmonize's session start nothing runs it. The 2-day stale threshold is fitted to that one gap (11-22 to 11-24).

## Verdict
**redirect.** The suggestion, ready for a prompt: "CL53b: (1) in `checkout_fresh`, move by itself only when HEAD is on the trunk; a branch with no commit of its own, or a detached HEAD, gets the line ('behind; it has no commit of its own: `git checkout main` if it is done') and is never switched; a worktree under .claude/worktrees/ is never moved. (2) Harmonize's SessionStart prints `kit.py fresh`'s line first (install adds it to a project's own session-start script, or the kit hook is chained from it); the orchestrator reruns it on ~/harmonize. Test: `scripts/review/CR-cl53-…-new-branch.py` leaves both checkouts where they were."
